name: eCourts Services — District & Taluka Courts (CIS National Core v3.2, portal v6)
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC / Department of Justice
geo_coverage: all-India district, sessions and taluka courts
lag: days (case data updated by courts near-real-time); FIR-to-case lag is months
caveats: Search-only interface: no bulk export, no pagination beyond a result set, every query CAPTCHA-gated.
CIS deployment date varies by establishment, so pre-2015 coverage is patchy in a geographically patterned way.
Cases filed from 2024-07-01 carry BNS/BNSS sections; earlier ones IPC/CrPC — one offence type splits into two series.
Only chargesheeted matters appear; police-closed and under-investigation FIRs never do.
Records name accused persons — republishing name-level data carries defamation and right-to-be-forgotten exposure.
evidence: Verified via primary artefacts on GitHub rather than the portal itself (egress proxy blocked all *.gov.in). Read working client code (neveonai-sys/mamlaAI) with verbatim constant BASE='https://services.ecourts.gov.in/ecourtindia_v6' and the full ?p= endpoint map: cnr_status/searchByCNR, casestatus/fillDistrict, casestatus/fillcomplex, casestatus/fillCourtEstablishment, casestatus/fillPoliceStation, casestatus/submitFirNo, casestatus/submitPartyName, casestatus/submitFillingNo, casestatus/submitAdvName, casestatus/fillCaseType, cause_list/submitCauseList, courtorder/submitCaseNo, courtorder/submitOrderDate, home/display_pdf. CAPTCHA served from /vendor/securimage/securimage_show.php.
how_to_obtain: Public, no login. Programmatic access requires solving a Securimage CAPTCHA and carrying a per-session app_token cookie/param. For volume, request bulk data from the High Court Registrar (Computer Cell) or the eCommittee instead of scraping.
notes: Endpoint map and CAPTCHA mechanics recorded in the .md dossier. Portal itself NOT fetched in this session — re-verify from an unblocked, ideally India-resident, network.

name: eCourts Case Status — Search by FIR Number (submitFirNo) + FIR Details block
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC
geo_coverage: all-India, wherever the court establishment populates the CIS FIR field
lag: FIR to court appearance: typically 2-12 months (post-chargesheet, post-cognizance)
caveats: THE CRITICAL CAVEAT: only chargesheeted cases reach court. Court counts are a LOWER BOUND on FIRs, biased by what police chose to charge — and that bias varies by state, crime head and station.
FIR Details is an optional CIS field; some establishments leave it blank or enter 0.
Police-station name string in the FIR block may not exactly match the fillPoliceStation dropdown label.
FIR numbers restart at 1 each calendar year per station, which makes enumeration bounded but also means (station, number, year) is the only valid key.
Full national enumeration is ~10^7 CAPTCHA'd requests — not feasible or advisable at Phase 2 scale.
evidence: Real captured eCourts case record, CNR KAHC010337682024, parses to fir: {state: KARNATAKA, district: BENGALURU, police_station: 'INDIRANAGAR PS', number: '155', year: 2024} (test/fixtures/case_details/KAHC010337682024.yml, openjustice-in/ecourts). Parser source case_details.py builds FIR(state=fir_details['State'], district=..., police_station=fir_details['Police Station'], number=..., year=...). POST parameters for submitFirNo read verbatim from working client: state_code, dist_code, court_complex_code, est_code, police_st_code, uniform_code, fir_no, firyear, case_status, fir_captcha_code, ajax_req, app_token. District-court case pages additionally carry 'Under Act(s)' and 'Under Section(s)' (observed example: IPC / 188).
how_to_obtain: Select state/district/court complex/establishment, fetch police station list, then POST submitFirNo with police_st_code+uniform_code (from a 'NN-NNNNNNN' dropdown value split on the first hyphen), fir_no, firyear, case_status and a solved CAPTCHA.
notes: This is the police<->court join key and the single most important finding in this domain. It makes the court system an indirect route to police-station-attributed crime records for states that publish nothing themselves — subject to the chargesheet filter above.

name: eCourts police-station master list (casestatus/fillPoliceStation)
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC
geo_coverage: all-India, enumerable per court establishment
caveats: No geometry and no coordinates — names and codes only. Needs an external gazetteer to be mappable.
One station appears under every establishment whose jurisdiction covers it; must be deduplicated on the uniform code.
Names are uppercase free text with PS / P.S. / POLICE STATION variants and transliteration inconsistency.
Whether uniform_code equals the CCTNS/NCRB uniform police-station code is a HYPOTHESIS, not verified.
evidence: Endpoint and parameters read from working client code: POST ?p=casestatus/fillPoliceStation with state_code, dist_code, court_complex_code, est_code, ajax_req, app_token; response key 'police_data'/'police_station_list' holds <option> elements whose value is a composite code, example '29-5137032', split on the first hyphen into police_st_code='29' and uniform_code='5137032'.
how_to_obtain: Walk the cascade fillDistrict -> fillcomplex -> fillCourtEstablishment and call fillPoliceStation for each establishment. Reference data only — no CAPTCHA observed on the cascade calls, unlike the case searches.
notes: Crawling this yields a national police-station registry with stable numeric codes. It is a crosswalk asset in its own right, far lower-risk than case scraping, and every other agent's work can join to it. Build it first.

name: CNR (Case Number Record) — national case identifier and its encoded geography
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC
geo_coverage: all-India
caveats: Encodes the COURT ESTABLISHMENT, i.e. where the case is heard, NOT where the offence occurred. Geocoding a CNR maps a courthouse, not a crime.
The state/district segment is the court's administrative district, which does not always match the revenue district or the police district.
Establishment codes are not published as a public master list; they must be enumerated from the portal cascade.
evidence: 16-character structure State(2) + District(2) + Court Establishment(2) + Filing serial(6) + Year(4), confirmed against a real record: CNR KAHC010337682024 = Karnataka High Court, establishment 01, serial 033768, year 2024, matching case CRL.P filing 5792/2024 in BENGALURU district. Lookup endpoint ?p=cnr_status/searchByCNR.
how_to_obtain: Public lookup at the portal; CAPTCHA-gated.
notes: Useful as a primary key and a state/district roll-up key. It is NOT a substitute for the FIR block's police station when the question is where a crime happened.

name: eCourts Services — High Courts (hcservices, CIS National Core v1.0)
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC
geo_coverage: all 25 High Courts and their benches
caveats: High Court criminal matters are appeals, revisions, bail and s.482 quashings — good for OUTCOME, near-useless for incidence.
Responses are '^^' and '^#' delimited strings, not JSON; 'INVALID CAPTCHA' in the first field signals retry.
Case-type and act numbering differs per court, so per-court code tables must be fetched before any act or case-type search.
evidence: BASE_URL = 'https://hcservices.ecourts.gov.in/ecourtindiaHC' with paths /cases/s_orderdate_qry.php, /cases/s_show_business.php, /cases/display_pdf.php, /cases/s_casetype_qry.php, /cases/s_actwise_qry.php, /cases/o_civil_case_history.php, /cases/case_no_qry.php, /cases/highcourt_causelist_qry.php — read verbatim from openjustice-in/ecourts ecourt.py. A recorded HTTP cassette shows a real POST body: action_code=showRecords&from_date=05-06-2024&to_date=05-06-2024&captcha=824mr&state_code=12&dist_code=1&__csrf_magic=sid%3A...  Securimage captcha markup confirmed in captured page HTML.
how_to_obtain: Public, CAPTCHA-gated. openjustice-in/ecourts (GPL-3.0) is a working single-threaded client.
notes: FIR-number search exists here too as a plain GET page (fir1.php) parameterised by state_cd/dist_cd/court_code.

name: National Judicial Data Grid — District & Subordinate Courts
publisher: Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice / NIC / eCommittee SCI
geo_coverage: all-India, 18,735 District & Subordinate and High Courts
caveats: Pendency and disposal are stock-and-flow measures of COURT LOAD, not of crime incidence. Never map pendency as crime.
Civil/criminal split only; no crime-head or act/section breakdown in the public dashboard.
Snapshot semantics — NJDG keeps no published historical series, so history only exists if we snapshot it daily ourselves.
Drill-down granularity in the UI reaches establishment level but the published aggregates are state and district.
evidence: Department of Justice page text, captured verbatim in a GitHub-hosted scrape of doj.gov.in: 'database of orders, judgments and case details of 18,735 District & Subordinate Courts and High Courts', 'Case data is available on NJDG for both civil and criminal cases with the ability to perform drill-down analysis based on the age of the case as well as the State and District', and case counts of 26.35 crore cases / 27.06 crore orders. Wikipedia confirms launch dates: District Courts 2015-09-19, High Courts 2020-07-03, Supreme Court 2023-09-14. Portal not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Public dashboard. Scrape and store dated snapshots to build a time series.
notes: Also carries a 'reasons for delay' field added recently, and land-records linkage for 26 states.

name: National Judicial Data Grid — High Courts
publisher: Department of Justice / NIC
geo_coverage: all 25 High Courts and benches
caveats: Bench-level geography, not district.
Snapshot only; no history published.
Court load, not crime.
evidence: URL given in the Department of Justice NJDG page text captured verbatim on GitHub: 'https://njdg.ecourts.gov.in/hcnjdgnew/ for NJDG High Courts'. Not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Public dashboard.

name: National Judicial Data Grid — Supreme Court
publisher: Supreme Court of India / NIC
geo_coverage: national
caveats: National only. No spatial value for a crime map.
Onboarded only in Sept 2023, so no depth of history.
evidence: URL given in the DoJ NJDG page text captured verbatim on GitHub; an alternate host scdg.sci.gov.in/scnjdg/ also appeared in search listings. Not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Public dashboard.
notes: Two candidate hosts seen (njdg.ecourts.gov.in/scnjdg/ and scdg.sci.gov.in/scnjdg/); confirm which resolves.

name: NJDG Open API (NDSAP) — government/institutional access only
publisher: Department of Justice, Ministry of Law & Justice
geo_coverage: all-India
caveats: NOT public. DoJ text: API 'has been provided to the Central & State Government ... using a departmental ID and access key' for 'institutional litigants'; public extension is only 'proposed'.
A private crime map is not an institutional litigant and will likely be refused.

Endpoint URLs circulating on GitHub (njdgnew/api/index.php, njdgnew/api/search with Bearer token) appear in LLM-generated projects with no evidence of a live response — treat as hallucinated until a 200 is observed.
No public documentation of the response schema was found.
evidence: Verbatim DoJ text (captured on GitHub from doj.gov.in): 'In consonance with the National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy (NDSAP) announced by the Government of India, Open Application Programming Interface (API) has been provided to the Central & State Government to allow easy access to the NJDG data using a departmental ID and access key. This will allow the institutional litigants to access the NJDG data for their evaluation and monitoring purposes. It is proposed to expand the facility to non-institutional litigants as well in future.' No API documentation page found; no working endpoint verified.
how_to_obtain: Write to the Department of Justice (eCourts Mission Mode Project), Ministry of Law & Justice, requesting a departmental ID and access key, naming an institutional user. Realistically requires partnering with a state Home Department, a State Legal Services Authority or a university. Fall back to daily scraping of the public dashboard.
notes: The lead that 'NJDG has an open API' is TRUE but materially misleading: it is open in the NDSAP sense (government-to-government), not in the public sense.

name: Judgements and Orders, Supreme Court and High Courts of India (judgments.ecourts.gov.in)
publisher: eCommittee, Supreme Court of India / NIC
geo_coverage: Supreme Court and all High Courts
caveats: Judgments and FINAL orders only — the tail of the process, not the caseload.
Appellate geography (bench), not incident geography.
Full-text PDFs of varying quality; older ones may be scanned.
No FIR field exposed in the search interface.
evidence: Search-result descriptions consistently report the portal's filter set as Bench, Case Type, Case Number, Year, Petitioner/Respondent Name, Judge Name, Act, Section, Decision date range, plus free-text search. Landing page not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Public search; CAPTCHA-gated.
notes: The Act + Section filter is the reason to care: it allows counting disposals by offence without NLP on judgment text.

name: Supreme Court of India — judgments and case status
publisher: Supreme Court of India
geo_coverage: national
caveats: National granularity. No mapping value.
Relevant only for doctrine and for pinning down outcome definitions.
evidence: URLs appeared consistently in search listings (sci.gov.in, sci.gov.in/judgements-case-no/). Not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Public.

name: Indian Kanoon — free Indian judgment search corpus
publisher: Indian Kanoon (private)
geo_coverage: Supreme Court, High Courts, tribunals, some district courts
caveats: Coverage skews to reported and appellate matters — the opposite of the volume crime a neighbourhood map is about.
No FIR field, no reliable police station, no geocode.
A paid API exists precisely to serve programmatic use; scraping the HTML site when that API exists is legally weaker and ethically worse.
Several Indian High Courts have ordered de-indexing of judgments naming acquitted persons — republishing text carries right-to-be-forgotten exposure.
evidence: Site and API referenced consistently across search results and multiple GitHub scraper projects. Not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Use the paid API (see indiankanoon-api entry) rather than scraping.

name: Indian Kanoon API
publisher: Indian Kanoon (private)
geo_coverage: Supreme Court, High Courts, tribunals, some district courts
caveats: Charged per search and per document call — cost scales with corpus size, so scope queries tightly.
Terms require a 'Powered by IKanoon' attribution wherever results are rendered to end users.
Judgment text is not structured crime data; extracting counts requires NLP with its own error rate.
evidence: Documentation at api.indiankanoon.org/documentation/ and terms at api.indiankanoon.org/terms/ reported consistently: four endpoint families (search, document, document fragments), JSON or XML selected by the HTTP Accept header, auth either by a shared API token generated on the site or by public/private key with per-request signing, per-call charging, and a 'Powered by IKanoon' attribution requirement. Pages not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Register on indiankanoon.org, generate an API token (or upload a public key), and pay per call.
notes: This is the clean, legal, documented route to judgment text. Prefer it over any scraping of the HTML site.

name: Development Data Lab — Indian Judicial Data (district courts, 2010-2018)
publisher: Development Data Lab
geo_coverage: all-India, 7,000+ district and subordinate courts, 80,000+ judges
caveats: NO FIR number and NO police station — both stripped in anonymisation. District (and court establishment) is the geographic floor.
Series stops at 2018. Useless for current conditions; essential as a nine-year baseline.
Non-commercial licence: a commercial crime map requires a separate licence from DDL. ShareAlike means derived datasets inherit the terms.
Scraped from eCourts, so it inherits every CIS coverage gap and the chargesheet filter — it is cases that reached court, not crimes that occurred.
Pre-BNS section codes only; needs an IPC<->BNS crosswalk to join to post-2024 data.
District identifiers predate a large wave of district creation since 2018 and must be remapped.
Reported totals differ by source: the DDL portal says 81M (25M criminal / 65M civil); the DDL team's own paper says the complete unfiltered release contains 77M case records. Reconcile on download.
evidence: Portal not fetched (egress blocked), but the file layout was verified from a downstream project's README: ddl_data/cases/cases_2010.dta ... cases_2018.dta, acts_sections.dta, and keys/ containing act_key.dta, section_key.dta, disp_name_key.dta, type_name_key.dta, purpose_name_key.dta, cases_state_key.dta, cases_district_key.dta, cases_court_key.dta — i.e. district AND court-establishment AND act AND section AND disposition keys all present. Size reported as ~15GB, Stata .dta. Dropbox data URL independently recorded in CivicDataLab teaching materials ('The database contains 81.2 million cases'). Variables per DDL's own description: filing, registration, hearing and decision dates; petitioner and respondent names; position of the presiding judge; acts and sections under which the case was filed; final decision/disposition.
how_to_obtain: Download the Dropbox folder linked from devdatalab.org/judicial-data. Researchers can apply to DDL for more extensive (less anonymised) access.
notes: The single best ready-made analytical asset in this domain and the only bulk, free, clean court dataset that exists for India. Ingest it first.

name: DDL replication package — In-group Bias in the Indian Judiciary (5M criminal cases)
publisher: Development Data Lab / Ash, Asher, Bhowmick, Chen, Devi, Goessmann, Novosad, Siddiqi
geo_coverage: all-India district and subordinate courts
caveats: Criminal subset (5M) built for a specific research question; filtering choices are the authors', not ours.
Requires Stata 16+, Python 3, Matlab 2019+ and ~30GB RAM to rebuild.
Ships a name->gender/religion neural classifier (97% out-of-sample). Applying identity inference to a public crime map would be a serious ethical failure — do not.
Same 2018 cutoff and same absence of FIR/police-station fields as the main DDL release.
evidence: Read the repository README: annual files named cases_clean_20XX in Stata format covering 2010-2018; judges_clean (judge demographics); poi_master (People of India); ACLED_India_violence_2005-2023; and district-level matching keys. Master build file make_justice.do. Data mirrored at Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/GHLGSW and on Google Drive. The paper text states the complete dataset, civil and criminal without filtering, contains 77 million case records, and notes that eCourts 'hosts the case records only through a slow search engine that returns unstructured results. The data was not previously available as a structured dataset or API.'
how_to_obtain: Download from Harvard Dataverse (preferred, stable DOI) or the linked Google Drive.
notes: Prefer the Dataverse copy for reproducibility. The 'district-level matching keys' are DDL's standard pc11-style keys, which is how this joins to census and to every other DDL dataset.

name: DAKSH — Deciphering Judicial Data / DAKSH database
publisher: DAKSH (Bengaluru)
geo_coverage: all-India district courts (selected)
caveats: Coverage and vintage not documented publicly; must be asked.
Value is as much methodological as data: DAKSH's cleaning rules are the published record of where eCourts data is internally inconsistent.
evidence: Described in a curated eCourts resource list (apoorv74/ecourts-india-resources datasets.md, read verbatim) as: 'various case and hearing related data available on e-courts are systematically cleaned, streamlined and pushed in the DAKSH's database', motivated by 'lot of inconsistencies in data that needs to be streamlined before proceeding with the analysis'. DAKSH site not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Contact DAKSH directly; they have collaborated with researchers and with the e-Committee.
notes: Read their cleaning methodology before writing any eCourts parser — it will save weeks.

name: Justice Hub — curated eCourts-derived research datasets
publisher: Justice Hub (CivicDataLab and partners)
geo_coverage: varies by dataset: Assam/Delhi/Haryana; Assam/Bihar/Jharkhand/Maharashtra/TN/UP; multi-state court complexes
caveats: Act-specific slices, not a general crime dataset — POCSO, child labour, contract enforcement.
Court-complex sampling, not full coverage: the contract-enforcement set covers roughly two cities per state.
Child-victim datasets (POCSO) demand strict suppression rules if anything derived from them is published.
evidence: Dataset table read verbatim from apoorv74/ecourts-india-resources datasets.md: (1) 'Unpacking Judicial Data to Track Implementation of the POCSO Act in Assam, Delhi & Haryana' — 'case details for the 19,783 cases registered in the district courts of Assam, Delhi and Haryana', all details downloaded from eCourts; (2) 'Analysis of Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986' — '10,800 cases registered since January 1, 2015, till March 2023' across Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh; (3) 'Data on Contract Enforcement Litigation' (NIPFP) — five acts, court complexes in about two cities per state. justicehub.in not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Public download from justicehub.in.
notes: These are the best available worked examples of act-specific eCourts extraction at scale, with published methodology. Read them before writing a scraper.

name: openjustice-in/ecourts — open-source eCourts scraping toolkit
publisher: Open Justice India (community)
geo_coverage: all High Courts and benches (district courts in progress)
caveats: GPL-3.0-or-later: linking it into our pipeline has licence consequences for anything we distribute.
Its own README: 'if you run this code, you are responsible for the legal implications of the same.'
District-court coverage and FIR-number search were listed as in development, not complete.
Deliberately single-threaded with no parallelism — by design, and we should not remove that.
evidence: Read the README and source. Entity model: Case(case_type, registration_number, cnr_number, filing_number, registration_date, first_hearing_date, decision_date, case_status, nature_of_disposal, coram, bench, state, district, judicial, petitioners[], respondents[], orders[], case_number, hearings[], category, sub_category, objections[], not_before_me, filing_date, fir, token); FIR(state, district, police_station, number, year). Ships a Securimage solver (captcha.py, THRESHOLD=0.4) and a retry loop with time.sleep(1) and up to 15 attempts, backing off on 5xx. README states the policy 'do not hammer the site' and that per-court case-type and act numbering must first be fetched via 'ecourts get-case-type' / 'ecourts get-act-type'.
how_to_obtain: pip install ecourts; source on GitHub.
notes: Adopt its rate-limiting ethic wholesale. Its test fixtures are themselves evidence of the eCourts record schema and are worth reading before designing our own parser. Publication cadence not stated by the publisher.

name: Prison Statistics India (PSI) — NCRB
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs
geo_coverage: all-India, all states and UTs
caveats: Published as state x jail-TYPE, not per named jail, in most tables; individual prison names appear only in some annexures.
Jail location is where a person is HELD, not where the offence occurred. Never map prison counts as neighbourhood crime.
Undertrial vs convict — the split that actually matters — is only state-level.
Definition and table-structure changes across years make the long series non-trivial to stitch.
PDF-first publication; scanned or image-heavy tables in older years.
evidence: PSI 2023 figures consistently reported: 1,332 prisons comprising 549 Sub Jails, 436 District Jails, 152 Central Jails, 101 Open Jails, 47 Special Jails, 35 Women Jails, 10 Borstal Schools and 2 other; total capacity 439,119; population 530,333 at 2023-12-31 (down from 573,220 in 2022); occupancy 120.8% (131.4% in 2022, 130.2% in 2021); Central Jails hold the largest capacity 198,150, then District Jails 172,074 and Sub Jails 43,800; highest occupancy in District Jails at 136.6%; 50.5% of undertrials in district jails and 37.6% in central jails; 65.5% of convicts in central jails. A PSI 2022 PDF URL was observed in search listings. ncrb.gov.in not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Free download from ncrb.gov.in. Tidy republished series are available from Dataful (dataful.in datasets 19003, 19004 and collection 1411) on a freemium basis, which saves substantial PDF parsing.
notes: FLAGGED: NCRB is covered in depth by another agent. Recorded here only for its jail geography, which is the prisons layer of this domain.

name: e-Prisons / National Prison Information Portal (NPIP)
publisher: National Informatics Centre / Ministry of Home Affairs
geo_coverage: participating states and UTs (not universal)
caveats: Dashboard only; no export observed and no API documented.
Not all states are on e-Prisons — some run their own prison management systems, so national coverage is incomplete and the gaps are not signposted.
Prisoner counts are custody, not crime. Mapping them as neighbourhood risk would be a category error.
Historical series not published; must be snapshotted.
evidence: Described consistently as NIC's prison suite: ePrisons MIS (internal, day-to-day prison operations), NPIP ('a citizen-centric portal showing statistical data of various jails in the country'), and Kara Bazaar. Functional modules listed as Prisoner Information Management System, Visitors Information Management System, Hospital Management System, Police Monitoring System, Courts Management System, Roaster Management System and Kiosk for Prison. Delivered as SaaS from NIC Cloud, free to adopt. Portal not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Public dashboard; scrape dated snapshots.
notes: The Courts Management System module implies e-Prisons already holds an internal prisoner<->case link, which would close the FIR -> case -> custody chain. Not public. Worth a targeted RTI.

name: e-Prisons MIS — per-prisoner operational records (internal)
publisher: National Informatics Centre / state Prisons Departments
geo_coverage: participating states and UTs
caveats: Per-prisoner personal data. Should never be public and we should not seek record-level access.
Aggregates only, via RTI, and even then jail-level counts of undertrials by offence head may be refused on privacy grounds.
evidence: Existence and module list inferred from NIC/e-Committee descriptions of the ePrisons Application Suite; no public interface seen.
how_to_obtain: RTI to the state DG (Prisons) / Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services, asking for jail-wise aggregate counts (capacity, undertrials, convicts, by major offence head, by year) and for the ePrisons data dictionary. Do not request record-level data.

name: State Prison / Correctional Services Department websites
publisher: State Home / Prisons Departments (36 states and UTs)
geo_coverage: per state
caveats: Quality is wildly uneven between states; several have no statistical publication at all.
Annual administration reports are often years behind and PDF-only.
Jail addresses, where published, are the practical route to a jail gazetteer — but they are inconsistent and rarely geocoded.
evidence: Not individually enumerated in this session — the WebSearch budget was exhausted and all .gov.in hosts were egress-blocked. Existence is certain (every state runs a Prisons Department); the per-state inventory is the work item.
how_to_obtain: Enumerate all 36 state/UT prison department sites; record per state whether a jail directory with addresses, and an annual administration report with statistics, exists.
notes: Primary purpose here is building a national jail gazetteer with coordinates, which is a clean, low-risk map layer.

name: Model Prison Manual 2016 and Model Prisons and Correctional Services Act 2023
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs / Bureau of Police Research and Development
geo_coverage: all-India (model law; states adopt individually)
caveats: Normative, not statistical.
Model law: adoption varies by state, so the categories it defines are not uniformly applied in practice.
evidence: Not fetched. Existence is well established; the exact MHA/BPRD hosting URL was not confirmed in this session (search budget exhausted, .gov.in blocked).
how_to_obtain: Download from mha.gov.in or bprd.nic.in.
notes: Defines the jail types, undertrial classes and reporting formats that PSI and e-Prisons use. Needed to read those sources correctly, not as data in itself.

name: State Directorates of Prosecution — conviction-rate and prosecution statistics
publisher: State Directorates of Prosecution / Home Departments
geo_coverage: per state; district-wise data exists internally
caveats: The DENOMINATOR is almost never stated: conviction rate over cases decided, over cases tried, or over FIRs registered? These differ by a large factor and are not comparable across states.
Figures are often announced politically rather than published as a series (e.g. a Chief Minister quoting 53%), which is not a dataset.
Rarely published below state level, though districts hold the underlying returns.
Prosecution was separated from police under CrPC s.25A at different dates in different states, breaking the series.
evidence: Maharashtra's Directorate of Prosecution publishes a conviction-rate page at dop.maharashtra.gov.in/conviction-rate (URL seen in search listings; not fetched, egress blocked). Reported figures encountered: Maharashtra 9% in 2013 rising to 53% in 2025 (per the Chief Minister); Tamil Nadu around 62%; a historical Directorate-of-Prosecutions range of 67.8% (Tamil Nadu) to 17.7% (Kerala).
how_to_obtain: RTI to each state Directorate of Prosecution for district-wise cases instituted / decided / convicted / acquitted by year and major offence head, 2015-2025, WITH the conviction-rate denominator definition stated in writing. District Government Pleader offices file these returns monthly, so the data exists.
notes: NCRB also publishes conviction rates nationally, at state level, on a consistent definition — cross-check any state figure against NCRB before using it.

name: NALSA statistics — legal aid, Lok Adalat, mediation, undertrial prisoners
publisher: National Legal Services Authority
geo_coverage: all-India, by State Legal Services Authority
caveats: Lok Adalat 'disposals' are overwhelmingly cheque-bounce, motor-accident claims, matrimonial and utility matters — NOT violent crime. Never read as crime resolution.
PDF tables with inconsistent structure between events and years.
State-level; DLSA (district) figures appear in some reports but not systematically.
Headline numbers are event totals, not a continuous series.
evidence: The statistics page is described as carrying reports on Lok Adalat, settlement through mediation, legal services beneficiaries, awareness camps and programmes, para legal volunteers, legal services clinics, victim compensation schemes, training programmes, and under trial prisoners. Scale example: the 3rd National Lok Adalat of 2026 settled over 2.10 crore cases with a cumulative settlement value of Rs 13,589.28 crore. nalsa.gov.in not fetched (egress blocked); Wikipedia's NALSA article carries no statistics.
how_to_obtain: Public PDF downloads.
notes: The 'undertrial prisoners' series is the one with real criminal-justice content — NALSA runs undertrial review committees at district level.

name: NALSA / SLSA victim compensation schemes and awards
publisher: National Legal Services Authority and State Legal Services Authorities
geo_coverage: all states and UTs, administered by DLSAs
caveats: Published only as aggregates; record-level data is victim-identifying and must never be sought or published.
Awards reflect who APPLIED and was granted, not who was victimised — severe and non-random under-application, worst for the most marginalised.
Scheme rates and eligibility differ by state, so amounts are not comparable across states.
Statutory basis moved from CrPC s.357A to BNSS s.396 in 2024 — check for a definition break.
evidence: NALSA victim-compensation page and state scheme pages (e.g. Madhya Pradesh SLSA) appeared in search listings, along with an application system at scourtapp.nic.in/lsams/nologin/victimcompensation.action (LSAMS). Schemes named include state schemes under CrPC s.357A and the NALSA Compensation Scheme for Women Victims/Survivors of Sexual Assault/other Crimes, 2018. Not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: RTI to each State Legal Services Authority for district-wise applications received, awards made, and amounts disbursed, by offence category and year. Also request the LSAMS data dictionary from NALSA.
notes: This is the only source in this domain keyed to the VICTIM and to offence category at district level. A genuinely different and underused view of serious crime, and a good complement to police-side counts.

name: Juvenile Justice Boards, Child Welfare Committees and NCPCR monitoring data
publisher: State Departments of Women & Child Development / SCPCRs / NCPCR
geo_coverage: all-India, one JJB and CWC per district
caveats: JJ Act 2015 s.74 legally bars publishing anything that could identify a child. Aggregate only, and suppress small cells.
JJB matters are largely ABSENT from the eCourts district-court CIS in most states, so the court route silently drops juvenile offending — a structural hole in the FIR->court chain.
NCRB 'Juveniles in conflict with law' tables are the only consistent national series and are state-level.
CWC data concerns children in need of care and protection, which is a different population from children in conflict with law — do not merge them.
evidence: Not fetched (search budget exhausted, .gov.in egress-blocked). Institutional structure is established by the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2015; NCPCR's existence and monitoring mandate are certain, the availability of district-wise JJB disposal data is not.
how_to_obtain: RTI to each state Department of Women & Child Development and SCPCR for district-wise JJB institution and disposal counts by offence head and year. Cross-check against NCRB's juvenile tables.
notes: FLAGGED: overlaps a child-protection / NCPCR agent. Recorded here because it is the gap in the court-outcomes chain, not because this agent owns it.

name: Open Courts in the Digital Age: A Prescription for an Open Data Policy (Vidhi)
publisher: Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy
geo_coverage: all-India
caveats: 2019 vintage; predates eCourts Phase III and the BNS transition.
Advocacy document, not data.
evidence: PDF URL seen in search listings alongside the finding that, despite the e-Committee's digitisation, 'the judiciary unfortunately lacks such a policy to share its data'. Not fetched (egress blocked).
how_to_obtain: Public PDF.
notes: The reference document for WHY bulk judicial data is unavailable and what a policy would look like. Cite it in every access request we send to a High Court Registrar or the e-Committee.
